Unlike sibling methods that may rely on Morton codes or spatial partitioning bounds, Point Location uses precomputed depth masks to determine the child octant index (0–7) directly from the destination coordinates using constant bitwise operations [S1, S2].

The claim states that Point Location uses precomputed depth masks to determine the child octant index (0–7) directly from destination coordinates using constant bitwise operations. Source [S1] explicitly states: 'By precomputing child bit depth[d]... and left-shifting by constants, we experience noticeably better performance. Then, we compute the target child octant with binary & and integer inequality operations. We &-mask this value with the destination coordinates and bit-shift by constants corresponding to the X,Y and Z components. This yields the 0-7 octant offset of the child, and hence its index.' Source [S2] corroborates this with identical descriptions. The claim accurately reflects the evidence provided in both sources.
